h1:
Nature Trip Itinerary
Khao Sam Roi Yot–Phraya Nakhon Cave–Three Bays
intro: Prachuap Khiri Khan packs in more nature than most people expect: limestone hills rising straight out of the sea, a cave with a royal pavilion inside, a lotus lagoon stretching to the horizon, and the Three Bays town where a single hilltop looks down on three bays at once. We've laid this out as a relaxed 3-day, 2-night trip that's easy with your own car, with a few early starts to beat the heat and the crowds — and the opening hours and entry fees are all checked for you.

blocks.html: Khao Sam Roi Yot was Thailand's first coastal national park, spread across the Sam Roi Yot, Kui Buri and Pranburi districts. It's about an hour's drive down from Hua Hin, and roughly an hour up from Prachuap town as well. The highlights sit fairly close together but are spread across several spots, so give yourself enough time. That's why this plan has you sleeping one night around Pranburi–Sam Roi Yot, then moving down to stay one more night in Prachuap town to cover the Three Bays.

blocks.title: Check the park entry fee before you go
blocks.html: Entry to Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park is 40 THB for Thai adults and 20 THB for children (200 THB for foreign adults, 100 THB for children). A single ticket covers several spots in the park on the same day — Laem Sala Beach, Phraya Nakhon Cave, the lotus lagoon and the Khao Daeng viewpoint — so hold onto it.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Climb Khao Daeng for the view, then into Phraya Nakhon Cave

items.activity: Leave your place around Pranburi/Sam Roi Yot and head for the Khao Daeng viewpoint
items.note: Go early — there's a hill to climb and the sun isn't fierce yet

items.activity: Hike up to the Khao Daeng viewpoint, with limestone hills and bays all around
items.note: The path is fairly steep, about a 40-minute to 1-hour climb. Wear trainers and bring water

items.activity: Drive to Ban Bang Pu to catch a boat or hike over the hill to Laem Sala Beach
items.note: A round-trip boat runs about 300 THB per boat (seats several people), or hike over the hill yourself, around 530 m

items.activity: Climb up to Phraya Nakhon Cave and see the Kuha Kharuehat royal pavilion
items.note: From the beach it's about another 500 m climb to the cave, steep going. The cave is open around 08:30–15:00

items.activity: Head back down for lunch at the seafood restaurants around Pak Nam Pran
items.note: From late morning to midday the light pours through the ceiling skylight and looks its best

items.activity: Rest and recharge, or stroll along Pranburi Beach
items.note: You'll have walked a lot today — get a good rest tonight

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: The lotus lagoon morning and evening, then move into Prachuap town

items.activity: Head to the lotus lagoon (Sam Roi Yot marsh) and walk the boardwalk to see lotuses and waterbirds
items.note: Cool air in the early morning and the waterbirds are out feeding — easy walking and photos on the boardwalk

items.activity: Take a boat out on the lagoon (if you want to get close to the lotus beds and bird flocks)
items.note: The boat is about 500 THB per boat, up to 6 people — well worth splitting

items.activity: Have lunch, then drive south into Prachuap town
items.note: It's about an hour from the park into town. Check in at your hotel first

items.activity: Climb Khao Chong Krachok and pay respects to the relics of the Buddha at the top
items.note: 396 steps, with monkeys along the way — keep any snacks well out of sight

items.activity: Take in the Three Bays view from the top of Khao Chong Krachok and wait for the evening light
items.note: The one spot where you can see Ao Noi, Ao Prachuap and Ao Manao all at once

items.activity: Have seafood in town and walk the Saranwithi pier along Ao Prachuap
items.note: The pier juts out into the sea — a nice spot for an evening breeze

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Ao Manao–Ao Noi before heading home

items.activity: Head to Ao Manao, a white-sand beach inside the Wing 5 air base
items.note: It's an air force area, so you swap your ID for a pass at the checkpoint — bring your ID card

items.activity: Stop by Ao Noi, a small quiet bay north of town
items.note: Fewer people than the other bays — a good spot to sit and listen to the waves before heading off

items.activity: Lunch in town and pick up Prachuap pineapples for the trip home
items.note: Prachuap pineapples are sweet and juicy — a good thing to take back
If you're heading north via Hua Hin, it's about 1.5 hours from town

items: A car — the spots are spread out and public transport is scarce, so driving yourself or renting a car is by far the easiest
Footwear — Khao Daeng, Khao Chong Krachok and Phraya Nakhon Cave all involve climbing, so wear trainers or hiking shoes
Sun and water — most of the route is out in the open, so pack a hat, sunscreen and plenty of drinking water
Cash — park fees, boat rides and many local shops mostly take cash
ID card — Ao Manao is inside the Wing 5 air base, so you'll swap your ID for a pass at the checkpoint before entering

blocks.title: Timing your visit to Phraya Nakhon Cave
blocks.html: The beam of light that drops through the ceiling skylight onto the Kuha Kharuehat pavilion looks its best from late morning to midday (roughly 10:00–12:00). If you want the shaft-of-light shot, aim to reach the cave right around then.

blocks.text: Extra stops if you have time to spare

items.name: Kaeo Cave
items.blurb: A cave of stalactites and stalagmites in the Chan valley, about 16 km from the park headquarters. Walking through takes around 2 hours — bring a flashlight

items.name: Khao Daeng canal cruise
items.blurb: A boat ride winding through mangrove forest and canals, watching local fishing life and waterbirds — great if you like quiet nature

items.name: Pak Nam Pranburi
items.blurb: A river mouth on the sea with seafood restaurants and a fish pier — a handy lunch stop midway through day one

faq.q: How many days do you need for Khao Sam Roi Yot and the Three Bays town?
faq.a: If you want to take in Phraya Nakhon Cave, the lotus lagoon, the Khao Daeng viewpoint and the Three Bays town without rushing, we'd suggest 3 days and 2 nights — one night around Pranburi–Sam Roi Yot, then move down for one more night in Prachuap town. With only a single day you'll probably have to pick just Phraya Nakhon Cave or the lotus lagoon, not both.

faq.q: What time does Phraya Nakhon Cave open, and how much is entry?
faq.a: The cave itself is open for visits around 08:30–15:00. Park entry is 40 THB for Thai adults and 20 THB for children (200/100 THB for foreigners). The boat from Bang Pu to Laem Sala Beach runs about 300 THB per boat, or you can hike over the hill yourself. Go from morning to midday so you catch the light through the skylight and get back before the cave closes.

faq.q: Is the climb up to Phraya Nakhon Cave hard?
faq.a: Fairly hard. From Laem Sala Beach it's about a 500 m climb up a steep, rocky path. Wear trainers, bring water and allow time for rest stops along the way. For anyone who genuinely can't manage it, there are porters who can carry your things or help you along on some sections.

faq.q: Is there anything special to prepare for Ao Manao?
faq.a: Ao Manao sits inside the air force's Wing 5 base, so you swap your ID for a pass at the checkpoint before entering — everyone should bring their ID card. Inside there's a clean white-sand beach and restaurants, making it a good stop on the morning of your last day before heading home.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to visit Khao Sam Roi Yot?
faq.a: Late rainy season into early cool season (roughly November to February) brings comfortable, cool weather, so the hill climbs aren't punishing, and the lagoon is full with the lotuses in bloom. In the rainy season the trails up the hills and into the cave can be slippery, so check the weather and the park's opening hours before you set off.
